subject: Order form proration, retroactive billing & withholding (Nimbus Health)
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 19 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Order form: Nimbus asks for proration/retroactive billing + withholding clause

Karthik / Lauren — quick heads-up from the Nimbus order form review: procurement pushed back on two commercial items in the attached redlines (Redwood_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf). High level: they want any ramp/proration applied retroactively to the start of the month (i.e., if they ramp on 15th, adjust the entire month), and they're insisting on an explicit withholding clause tied to their state-level tax rules.

Why this matters: retro proration increases our short-term revenue risk if they ramp late in the billing period. Withholding introduces payment timing/collection complexity and may require gross-up language or tax residency evidence.

Proposed immediate actions:
- Karthik: can you propose a commercial compromise on proration (e.g., proration applies only prospectively from the next invoice) and share an updated Pricing_Schedule_Nimbus_v2.xlsx?
- Lauren: please advise on acceptable language for withholding (we typically provide tax residency letter / W-9 or W-8BEN-E equivalents and resist gross-up requests unless compelled).
- I'll coordinate with our finance team to confirm net terms flexibility and invoice cadence (monthly in arrears vs. monthly pro forma).

Attached: Redwood_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf (customer redlines), Pricing_Schedule_Nimbus_v2.xlsx (draft pricing adjustments).

Thanks — Soojin

--
Soojin Lee

Thanks Soojin — attaching our redline highlights for clarity (we flagged the proration and a withholding requirement as must-haves for our internal approval).

To clarify our position: 1) Proration: our legal/finance team requires that if usage ramps within a billing month we reconcile to the actual monthly committed level for that same month. This is standard for our vendor SaaS agreements. 2) Withholding: certain state healthcare payers require us to withhold a small portion of payments unless vendors provide proof of tax residency / EIN. We can share PO # NH-2026-771 once commercial terms are agreed.

We can be flexible on net terms if Redwood can provide the tax evidence and agree to prospective proration for future quarters, but we need the withholding language in the order form to pass procurement today.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Summers <purchasing@nimbushealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Dec 2026 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form: Nimbus asks for proration/retroactive billing + withholding clause

Ava — thanks for the clarity and the PO reference. Short reply with a commercial compromise we can sign off on internally: 

1) Proration: Redwood proposes proration be applied prospectively. For any ramp month we will bill actual usage for that month; any minimum commit adjustments (credited or invoiced) will start on the next invoice period. This avoids revenue clawback and aligns with our billing system. If Nimbus needs retroactive reconciliation for internal reporting, we can provide a usage report, but we cannot provide account-level credits that change historical invoice totals beyond 30 days after invoice issuance.

2) Withholding: we can accept a withholding acknowledgement clause that says "Customer may withhold taxes required by law; Customer shall provide Redwood with a copy of the withholding notice and supporting tax form." We prefer to avoid gross-up obligations. To avoid withholding entirely, Redwood can provide tax residency evidence (EIN, W-9/W-8). We will attach Redwood_Tax_Residency_Letter.pdf and a copy of the W-9/W-8 equivalent for your team.

3) Net terms & invoicing: Redwood can accept Net45 for this deal (request from Redwood finance is Net30 as standard), provided we receive PO NH-2026-771 and an executed order form. Invoice cadence will be monthly in arrears; payment due Net45 from invoice date.

I'll attach an updated Pricing_Schedule_Nimbus_v2.xlsx reflecting a small ramp credit structure (see tab 'RampCredit') and a redlined Order Form with prospective proration language. Can you confirm whether PO will be issued against the final signed order form?

Next steps: Lauren — can you propose final contract language on withholding and the 30-day invoice adjustment cap?

Thanks,
Karthik

--

Karthik — appreciate the fast turnaround. A few notes from finance:
- Net45 is acceptable for legal review if Redwood accepts the withholding clause language and provides the tax residency evidence.
- On proration: our controller still prefers reconciliation to the month-of usage; given your proposed prospective approach, we'd need a written confirmation that you will provide a monthly usage statement within 5 business days of month-end.
- We will not issue the PO until the order form has the withholding acknowledgement and the usage-statement commitment.

Could you send the usage statement sample and the tax evidence as soon as possible? Also confirm whether invoices will include a line-item showing any withheld amount and supporting withholding notice in the invoice package.

Thanks — I'll aim to get procurement's sign-off once we have those pieces.

Ava

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Summers <purchasing@nimbushealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Dec 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Order form: Nimbus asks for proration/retroactive billing + withholding clause

Ava / Karthik — looping in legal and confirming Redwood's position and next steps below.

1) Withholding language: proposed contract clause (for insertion into Order Form):
"Customer may deduct or withhold amounts from payments only to the extent required by applicable law. Customer shall promptly provide Redwood with written notice of any withholding requirement and provide official supporting documentation. Where practicable, Customer shall cooperate to minimize withholding. Unless required by law, Customer shall not be obligated to gross-up amounts withheld."

2) Proration / invoice reconciliation: we accept a monthly usage statement commitment (Redwood will deliver a CSV summary and PDF statement within 5 business days after month-end). However, adjacency to invoices: Redwood will not re-open invoices older than 30 days for crediting/rebilling except in cases of provider error confirmed by Redwood. That should be sufficient operational control.

3) Tax evidence / residency: we will provide a Redwood_Tax_Residency_Letter.pdf and a W-9/W-8 copy. Finance will add an EIN on the letter. Those documents will be provided as part of the execution package — see attached Tax_Evidence_W9_W8_COPY.docx.

4) Invoice content: Redwood will show withheld amounts as a separate line item and attach the withholding notice if provided by Customer. If withholding causes short payment, Redwood will follow up and agree on a cure path (payment of remaining balance or documentation to reclaim withheld funds).

If the above is acceptable, please confirm and we'll prepare a final redline for signature (DocuSign link to follow).

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com

Attachments referenced: Redwood_Tax_Residency_Letter.pdf, Tax_Evidence_W9_W8_COPY.docx
